notes: Workflow/planning skill — output is a clarify-then-plan artifact, not shipped code. Dry-run prompts ask the agent to plan (not implement) a net-new whip feature; graded on whether it clarifies ambiguity, checks docs/roadmap.md + docs/features.md + docs/learnings/ for prior art before designing, names concrete files across the five surfaces (tools / agent loop / TUI / config / session store), plans channel-idiomatic concurrency with -race tests, plans the docs/features.md section + roadmap checkbox, and ends at task check + adversarial review rather than jumping into code.

evals.name: mcp-server-support
evals.prompt: I want whip to support MCP servers so the agent can call tools from configured MCP servers (stdio and HTTP), backwards compatible with claude-style .mcp.json config.
evals.expected_output: Clarifies the ambiguity (which transports in v1, config precedence vs claude/codex formats, tool name prefixing, what happens when a server is down at startup, whether subagents inherit MCP tools). Checks docs/roadmap.md and docs/learnings/ for existing MCP research before designing. Plans a new internal/mcp package (config normalization, client manager, tools.Tool adapter) that plugs into agent.New via the existing Tool{Def,Run} contract — not a parallel tool registry. Names concrete files, plans tool output truncation via the existing maxOutput convention, per-call timeouts, lazy/background connect so a dead server can't block startup. Addresses concurrency: MCP calls in parallel tool batches, goroutine ownership on server shutdown, -race tests with an in-process fake MCP server. Plans a /mcp slash command in the existing command() switch, docs/features.md section, and task check + adversarial review. Does NOT start coding before plan sign-off and does NOT hand-wave the config-compat question.

evals.name: diff-view-for-edit-tool
evals.prompt: Add a diff view for edit tool results so I can see what changed inline in the transcript.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is already on docs/roadmap.md with cited prior art (pi's edit tool details {diff, patch, firstChangedLine}; opencode's split-vs-unified by terminal width >120) and plans the port with citations rather than designing from scratch. Clarifies (unified vs split, color, expand/collapse interaction with the existing blockTool ctrl+e mechanism). Plans: edit tool returns/renders diff info, a transcript block change in internal/tui with width-dependent rendering + resize re-render, headless TUI tests following tool_expand_test.go/resize_test.go patterns, the docs/features.md section, and checking the roadmap box in the same change. No new dependency without justification (considers whether a minimal unified-diff can be computed in-repo).

evals.name: session-fork-command
evals.prompt: Add a /fork command that branches the current session so I can explore an alternative direction without losing my place.
evals.expected_output: Clarifies (fork = copy messages into a new session id? share prefix? what happens to goal/state/usage totals? does the fork show in /resume?). Identifies the five-surface split: agent (copying Agent.Messages), session store (new row via Store.Create + Save semantics, incremental from-index), TUI (/fork case in the command() switch + transcript notice), config untouched. Plans resume round-trip tests (fork then --resume both sessions), asks about message Authored markers surviving the copy, and keeps it minimal — no fork tree UI in v1, marked ponytail if deferred. Writes the .ai-docs plan, waits for sign-off, plans task check + -race + adversarial review.
